title: Cycle-length distribution differs between life-themed and consciousness-themed ECA rules at n=4 ring
question: Across all 16 starting states of an n=4 periodic ring, do life-themed rules (30, 110) have a HIGHER mean cycle length than consciousness-themed rules (105, 150)?
engine: pure hexa-lang (no IIT4); deterministic 20-step forward orbit + first-repeat detection (cycle length = index gap between first appearance and reappearance)
runtime: $0 pool ubu-2 · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic byte-identical

rule_30_life.note: chaotic class III · longest mean cycle

rule_110_life.note: universal class IV but at n=4 cycle collapses to 1.75

rule_105_consc.note: consciousness class — IDENTICAL to rule_110 here

rule_204_anchor.note: identity rule (sanity) — every state fixed → L=1

rule_0_anchor.note: null rule (sanity) — collapses to 0 fixed point

falsifier_eval.F328_3_NOT_DRIVEN_BY_ONE_RULE: FAIL — rule_30 alone produces the spread (6.25 vs 1.75); rule_110 ties consc class exactly. The mean-aggregate masks a within-life heterogeneity.
falsifier_eval.F328_4_ANCHORS_NON_TRIVIAL: PASS — identity/null both give mean_L=1.0 distinct from all live rules ≥1.75

verdict_derived: 🟢 SUPPORTED-NUMERICAL (CONDITIONAL) — aggregate ratio 2.29× passes the H1 threshold but the F328.3 within-class heterogeneity falsifier exposes that the difference is driven entirely by rule_30. Three of four live rules (110/105/150) share mean_L=1.75 exactly. So 'life > consciousness on cycle length' holds at the chosen panel mean, but the underlying separator is NOT life-vs-consciousness — it is rule_30's chaotic class III alone. Publishable conditional support: H1 aggregate-PASS but mechanistically driven by a single rule.
structural_vs_dynamical: DYNAMICAL kernel (forward timestep + cycle detection) at n=4 scale — yet rule_110/105/150 collapse to identical cycle structure, consistent with H_327's finding that n=4 ECA is too small for non-trivial dynamical separation except in the chaotic regime (rule 30)
honest_limits: n=4 ECA panel; rule 110's 'universal class IV' character only emerges at larger n
Single class-mapping (life ⊃ {30,110} · consc ⊃ {105,150}) inherited from H_287/H_320 literature; alternative mappings (e.g. moving rule 110 into consc) would flip the verdict
Cycle length is just one orbit descriptor; cycle COUNT (number of distinct attractor cycles) is a complementary axis not measured here
Anchor sanity (rule_204/0 → mean_L=1.0) confirms the kernel is non-tautological but does not address the F328.3 heterogeneity
